{{Cuisine of Indonesia}}
'''Gorontalese cuisine''' or '''Gorontalo cuisine''' is the traditional cuisine of the [[Gorontalo people|Gorontalese People]] of the [[Gorontalo|Gorontalo Peninsula]], North [[Sulawesi|Sulawesi island]], Indonesia.<ref>Noho, Y., Husain, D. and Kadir, R., 2020, December. Gastronomic Tourism Development in Gorontalo Province. In ''Proceedings of International Interdisciplinary Conference on Sustainable Development Goals (IICSDGs)'' (Vol. 3, No. 1, pp. 41-47).</ref> It is also known as ''Hulontalo'' cuisine by ''perantauan'' (migrating) Gorontalo people, after "Hulontalo", the name for Gorontalo in the [[Gorontalo language]]. 

Gorontalese cuisine is known for its fresh [[seafood]], and liberal use of [[Spice|spices]] and [[Herb|herbs]].<ref>Albala, K. ed., 2016. ''At the Table: Food and Family around the World: Food and Family around the World''. ABC-CLIO.</ref>

The strategic location of Gorontalo, with the [[Celebes Sea]] and [[Pacific Ocean]] to the north and the [[Gulf of Tomini]] to the south, made the Gorontalo region a strategic shipping route in the past. This history has formed the roots of a unique and distinctive culture in Gorontalo, including its unique dishes. 

Along with the division of Gorontalo into a province and its separation from [[North Sulawesi]], Gorontalo's cuisine has become an increasingly popular and well-recognized as part of [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesia's national culinary heritage.]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-10 |title=Exploring the Land of Spices, Discovering the Taste of Gorontalo |url=https://www.worldfoodtravel.org/news-exploring-the-land-of-spices-discovering-the-taste-of-gorontalo |access-date=2023-07-07 |website=www.worldfoodtravel.org |language=en}}</ref>
